newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Ross urges Israeli-PLO security partnership.
newsitem.headline: Ross urges Israeli-PLO security partnership.

text.p: U.S. envoy Dennis Ross urged Israelis and Palestinians on Monday to work as partners against a "common threat" from militants following a suicide attack in Jerusalem that has plunged peacemaking deep into crisis.
Ross, on the second day of his mission, said the two sides had come a step closer to reviving security ties but cautioned that success would be measured by results.
"We're not looking for meetings as an end in themselves. We're looking for results," Ross told reporters after talks with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
"Security is something that serves Israeli interests and Palestinian interests. You have a common threat and you have a common enemy and it's important to deal with that as partners."

Within hours of his arrival on Sunday, Ross had brought together Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli officials for the first time since two Arab suicide bombers brought carnage to Jerusalem's main Jewish market on July 30.
The death toll from the attack rose to 16, including the two Moslem militants, with the death in hospital on Monday of a 49-year-old Israeli man who was gravely injured in the blast.
PLO officials said the U.S.-Israeli-PLO meeting late on Sunday had enabled the sides to exchange information on the attack and to coordinate security.

A second meeting, among Israeli, Palestinian and American security officials, was set for Monday night but neither Israel nor the Palestinians sounded confident that progress towards salvaging peace efforts would come swiftly.
"We are insisting that the main issue is the political issue," Arafat adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah told Israel Radio.
"Unless they understand there is a peace agreement signed by the Palestinian Authority and the Israeli authorities, unless it's implemented fully and accurately, the crisis will carry on," he said.
Mordechai said the peace process could not move forward until Arafat did "what is necessary to fight against terrorism".
"We are waiting for the real cooperation between our security people and their security people," he said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has accused Arafat of having a "revolving door" for militants in his prisons.
He has conditioned a resumption of peace talks and an easing of economic and security sanctions imposed on the West Bank and Gaza Strip after the bombings on a crackdown by the Palestinian Authority.

In Amman, the Islamic militant group Hamas warned Arafat against heeding Israel's demands. "It would be dangerous, not just for him...It would lead to Palestinians fighting Palestinians," Hamas spokesman Ibrahim Ghoshe said.

Netanyahu said on Sunday that Israel had growing indications that Hamas carried out the attack even though Israeli and Palestinian officials had questioned the authenticity of a Hamas claim of responsibility.
In Gaza City, thousands of Palestinian protesters marched down the main street demanding Israel free their imprisoned sons and end the closure imposed on Palestinians after the attack.
Trouble also flared briefly just outside the Palestinian-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah when about 50 youths burned tyres and tried to throw stones at Israeli soldiers.
Palestinian police entered Israeli-controlled territory to disperse the protesters.

Ross said he did not expect to stay "too much longer" but did not elaborate. He has been preparing for U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's first trip to the region, expected at the end of the month provided progress is made on security.
"There has to be a basis of security to be able to underpin and move the peace process and there has to be a political dimension ultimately for the peace process to succeed," Ross said.
Arafat says he has met his responsibilities on security and accuses Netanyahu of using the Jerusalem bombings as an excuse to inflict "collective punishment" on Palestinians.

Peace talks had already been in crisis over a Jewish settlement Israel began building in Arab East Jerusalem in March. Palestinians want construction halted and an end to Palestinian house demolitions and land confiscations as well as a lifting of the closure.
